title: My AI-assisted boxing game Punchies is in free beta — from a Claude prototype to Codex and Modern controls
author: No_Barracuda_2784
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/j987v9rnvgvh1.png?width=1920&format=png&auto=webp&s=935f89de894a77b1c10026cbebf81015f655ae03

I’m the developer of Punchies, a browser boxing game that started with two fighters viewed from above and a wooden dummy to test punches on. It’s now in free beta, and I wanted to share how the AI workflow changed as it grew.

Claude handled the initial prototype and proof of concept. Once the art came in, development shifted to Codex, working through the game’s implementation and iterations. Gemini’s Lyria was used to make the background music. I directed the design decisions and what to change as the project developed.

Two of the biggest gameplay turns were developing the charged uppercut into a clearer Super system, then introducing Modern controls. Modern lets you focus on movement, range and timing with Normal Attack and Super; Classic keeps the individual punches, guard, dodge and stamina management. The aim is to make that first exchange easy to get into while still giving you reasons to circle, bait a punch and wait for an opening.

You can fight AI opponents, play local versus or try online matches. The beta starts with Marco, Mia and Bruno, with Roxy and Nadia unlocked by completing matches. It’s free, with no ads, shop or XP progression.

Playable beta: [https://polsia.itch.io/punchies-beta-test](https://polsia.itch.io/punchies-beta-test)

I’m particularly interested in whether Modern controls make sense without much explanation, and whether you can tell when you’re in range. If you try it, I’d love to hear where the controls feel clear or confusing. For other devs using AI, how do you judge when a mechanic is ready to move beyond the prototype?
